newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenspan vigil hampers uneven German share mkt.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan vigil hampers uneven German share mkt.

text.p: The German share market inched up to post minor gains on Wednesday amid selective interest in chemical stocks, but the mood was cautious ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony.
The 30-share DAX index rose 4.66 points to end the floor session at 3,237.87 points, having spent the session mired in a 10-point range.

Dealers said many were keeping out of the action until it was clear what Greenspan's views on market developments were, after the Fed chairman last year sparked a global mini-crash on markets by warning against their "irrational exuberance".
"We need him to say something more positive, in fact anything positive at all would help," said a dealer at a major Frankfurt bank. "The word 'normalisation' is what I'll be looking for."
Volumes were low and the overall market uneven, with some pressure on dollar-sensitive shares because of the dollar's slide to below 1.67 marks.
Among auto stocks, dollar-driven Daimler-Benz was down 1.90 marks at 120.75 marks, while Volkswagen was down 6.50 marks at 791.50 after reporting disappointing 1996 results Tuesday.
The outperformer of the day was pharmaceutical company Schering, which surged to a new all-time high of 155 marks and ended with gains of 6.80 marks at 153 marks.

Dealers said speculation that Japan may remove its ban on the Pill plus reports that the company expected higher sales in certain niches had lifting the shares to levels that also promoted technically driven buying interest.
The Financial Times had cited a Japanese government report saying contraceptive pills, a core business area for Schering, were safe and effective.

Among other outperformers, chemical firm Henkel advanced as much as five percent to 86 marks and Fresenius Medical Care rose seven marks to 158 marks -- amid what dealers said was renewed technically-driven interest in smaller chemical shares.
